The below is a rebuttal to any issuance change that aims to target a specific ratio:

My concern is the same it has been since this began-

A reduction in staking APR will hurt decentralized home stakers before it meaningfully reduces centralized staking. The opportunity cost for centralized custodians is near zero and the realized costs of home stakers are substantial. 

Yes, some zealots will run net negative but they will be diluted by the centralized custodians. 

This seems self evident to me with *any* form of targeting that connects issuance with an idealized staking ratio. 

If our goal is to make ETH maximally decentralized and minimally inflationary we should think about ways to mitigate the need for stakers and bonds all together. If our goal is maximum decentralization alone, then we seem to be in a fine place and should perhaps consider a partially enshrined rainbow staking system.

Nice profile pic :-)

What forms of decentralization are you considering here? There's a strong emotional effect behind waving decentralization and it's often used to avoid first, second and third order arguments and realities.
Here are a couple of dimensions to consider, Decentralization as in:
 - as many validating nodes as possible
 - as geographically spread out as possible
 - as diverse in their operator as possible
 - as diverse in their actual owner (the party providing the 32ETH) as possible 
 - as diverse in their software (client diversity) as possible 
 - as diverse as possible in validating power (Nakamoto Coefficient - how many independent entities are required to control a critical share)
in parallel of those dimensions, when looking at their perceived or realised level of decentralization, we have to take in consideration the barrier to entry for each of those dimentions - how easy/hard it is for a new validator to enter:
- what are the entry or exit costs?
- what are the sunk costs?
- is the same level of technology available to incumbent businesses and new entrants?
This boils down to the contestability of the validator set. 

Let's look at this argument against a change in issuance "reducing issuance will push solo stakers out and reduce Ethereum decentralization" and follow up on its logic, why not doubling the staking rewards if we believe it will help Solo Staker? I highly doubt anyone will thread towards that because the security implications of too many ETH at stake will be too heavy to bear.
Are we better off in a situation where :
A - half the supply of ETH is at stake, half of the ETH at stake are handled by 5 entities, 5% of the ETH at stake are handled by solo stakers,
or 
B - 20% of the supply of ETH is at stake, 40% is handled by 5 entities, 15% handled by solo stakers.

It's fair to say that no one would prefer A over B and that we are currently trending fast towards A. 
Nevertheless many stand biased towards conservatism, adamently defending the current issuance rate because it is the status quo. Ethereum has no history of status quo promotion regarding issuance, we drastically changed it several times. 

It's also fair to say that we currently still lack the definitive data to establish reaction functions of solo stakers and institutional stakers. It is therefore very handy to just say "this is bad for decentralization" or "this is harmful to solo stakers". Nevertheless this is absolutely not a reason to delay acting on it.

We can say with very high confidence for institutional money that it will always favor the lowest risk highest rewards option. Right now this is in Staking, it will be in staking forever if we dont do anything and that's skewed towards higher market share for centralized parties.

@EthStaker has been the main voice for solo stakers through their annual survey: a meaningful and growing minority of solo stakers (35% in 2025, up from 21% in 2024) actively factor ETH supply inflation into their staking decisions. Many explicitly value ETH-as-money over staking yield. The 'cut issuance kills solo stakers' frame, in particular, is contradicted by the 84% who say they wouldn't even leave for higher LST yields (2026 data is coming, see https://t.co/VbFRklPaXF ).

I would actually argue that:

Not changing the issuance is very much killing solo stakers, damaging decentralization, constantly lowering their market share, hurting the value of their principal (the 32ETH) to the profit of staking services that have less consideration over the principal valuation and are mainly driven by the fees extracted from the staking rewards.

Let's not forget why core devs and protocol researchers are supporting issuance reduction for security reasons, notably for the credibility of large slashing events.

Here's another pack emotional arguments: 
I am a solo staker and I've been staking since 1st of Dec 2020. I will continue to stake as long as my yield is positive. I worry about the security and credible neutraliy of Ethereum, I worry about the $1bn we are wasting every year in over paying for our security, I worry about the attractivity of DeFi versus the staking yield.

Thank you! And fully agree on the multidimensional nature of decentralization! It’s why I emphasize home stakers rather than solo stakers. It encompasses  broader set and has more nuance. I’m a fan of Nixo’s executive control model. 

Halving the issuance being bad does not imply doubling issuance must be good. I would argue that high issuance and near 0 issuance rates are both harmful to home stakers. It does not have to be a linear relationship. 

My main critique is against issuance rates that lead to negative home staker APR. You seem to share this concern - “ I will continue to stake as long as my yield is positive. “

The croissant curve and other curves that target a certain ratio of stake do so punitively in a way that requires negative real rates for home stakers but not for centralized stakers. Centralized operators already run at a profit with 0% take rate on their  stake - how can we stop such entities from dominating in the APR range below break even (~0.8%/yr)?

name: Evan 🦇🔊

full_text:
You can’t control the power of deflation and the burn. You can control the issuance. What matters is positive nominal yield bc the differential is how much better is it to stake at home vs hold ETH. 

You get all the benefits of deflation simply by holding the ETH. The question of staking is downstream. 

For example, if real yield is 2.1% on staked ETH but 2% of that is in the burn, then the 0.1% boost to running a node is insignificant to the cost and effort of running a node.
